reference.title: Barbell Overhead Squat
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold it down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.3 s up

prescription.load: Light: start with a PVC pipe or empty bar; add load only while the bar stays over mid-foot with locked arms.
prescription.progression: Add 1-2.5 kg when every rep is full depth with the bar over the feet.

cues.text: Press or jerk the bar overhead with a wide snatch grip, elbows locked, armpits turned forward, shoulder blades shrugged up into the bar. Bar over the middle of the foot, slightly behind the head; feet about shoulder width, toes out.
Big breath, brace, and sit straight down between the heels while pushing up into the bar; the chest stays tall and the bar stays over mid-foot.
Hips below the knees if you can keep the bar over mid-foot, the arms locked and the heels down; hold briefly.
Stand up while pressing the bar to the ceiling; keep the arms locked and the bar over the feet. Breathe out past the hardest part.
Stand tall with the bar locked out, breathe and brace for the next rep.

mistakes.mistake: Bar drifting forward of the feet
mistakes.fix: Push the head and chest through the arms so the bar stays over mid-foot; reduce depth until you can.
Lock the elbows and push up into the bar the whole rep; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Trunk folding forward at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Work on ankle, hip and upper-back mobility; squat only as deep as you stay upright.
Keep the whole foot down; a small heel lift or lifting shoes help.
Use a snatch-width grip so the bar can sit over the feet with locked elbows.

kinematics.setup: 44 cm between the ankle centres (≈1.1x the rig's 40 cm shoulder width), toes out 25°
kinematics.norm: About shoulder width with the toes out (Lorenzetti 2018)

kinematics.peak: ≈124°; hip joints 5.7 cm below the knee joints

kinematics.norm: Large at depth, with the trunk kept upright (Aspe 2014)
More upright than the back squat to keep the bar over the feet (Aspe 2014)

kinematics.setup: Overhead on locked arms (elbow 3.2-3.6°), 96 cm snatch grip (handle centres), 33.8 cm above the head-neck joint
kinematics.peak: Bar 0 cm from mid-foot, within 0.4 cm fore-aft all rep; shoulder elevation ≈120° standing, ≈111° at the bottom (bar + body centre of mass 4.4 → -1.8 cm)
kinematics.norm: Bar overhead on locked arms, kept over mid-foot (common coaching; Aspe 2014)

kinematics.peak: 2.2 s down, 0.4 s pause, 1.3 s up, 1.3 s reset
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Overhead Squat, video (movement reference only)
Aspe & Swinton 2014, electromyographic and kinetic comparison of the back squat and overhead squat (J Strength Cond Res 28(10):2827-2836)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Lorenzetti et al. 2018, how to squat: stance widths, foot angles and experience (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil)
Larsen et al. 2021, stance width and bar placement in back squats: kinematics, kinetics and EMG (Front Sports Act Living)

cautions: Learn it with a PVC pipe or empty bar first; the load is limited by shoulder and trunk control, not leg strength.
If you lose the bar, push it away and step out (forward or back) rather than trying to save it; practise this with a light bar and bumper plates on a platform.
Avoid if you have shoulder pain overhead or cannot lock the arms straight with the bar over the feet.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Limited shoulder or ankle mobility: widen the grip, use a small heel lift or reduce depth.
regressions: Overhead squat with a PVC pipe.

muscleNotes.calves_l: Control the forward travel of the knees.
